::: {.callout-note .legacy appearance="simple"}
This post is from the blog I kept as Preceptor in Mathematics at Harvard (2005–2008). It's kept here as an archive; some links are dead and references are dated.
:::

Spotted in my multiple RSS feeds today:

- [Darren Kuropatwa](http://adifference.blogspot.com/2007/09/global-learners.html) on the [The Global Learners](http://principianteglobal.blogspot.com/) blog. Darren does great stuff with Web 2.0 in a high school mathematics classroom
- [Large integers. *[Really]{.T1}*](http://www.cs.grinnell.edu/~stone/essays/large-integers/large-integers.xhtml)[ [large.](http://www.cs.grinnell.edu/~stone/essays/large-integers/large-integers.xhtml) A history of the names for large numbers, large numbers appearing in the literature, and a contest to find the largest integer you can fit on a postcard.]{.T2}
- [Dangerous Knowledge](http://video.google.com/videoplay?docid=-3503877302082311448) In this one-off documentary, David Malone looks at four brilliant mathematicians - Georg Cantor, Ludwig Boltzmann, Kurt Gödel and AlanTuring- whose genius has profoundly affected us, but which tragically drove them insane and eventually led to them all committing suicide.
- [Getting to Grips with LaTeX](http://www.andy-roberts.net/misc/latex/index.html) - LaTeX Tutorials by Andrew Roberts @ School of Computing, University of Leeds
- The [hidden flight simulator in Google Earth](http://feeds.macosxhints.com/~r/macosxhints/recent/~3/153462428/article.php)
- The all-knowing Wikipedia on [Quaternions](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quaternion)
- The Boston area VC firm that [took a pass on Facebook](http://www.boston.com/business/technology/articles/2007/09/09/why_facebook_went_west/)
